title: Vegan lemon drizzle cake
subtitle: plant-based lemon drizzle with sharp lemon syrup crust
excerpt: A vegan lemon drizzle uses plant milk and vegan butter to produce the same moist, crisp-topped loaf as the classic version. The drizzle, lemon juice and sugar poured over while the cake is still warm, soaks in and forms the slightly crystalline crust that defines a good lemon drizzle. Nothing about the method or the result is compromised by leaving out the eggs; the texture is close-crumbed and springy.
sourceNotes: The lemon drizzle cake in its current form is a firmly established British classic, associated most strongly with Nigella Lawson's 2000 recipe which drove its widespread adoption as a home staple. Vegan adaptations became mainstream from about 2015 onward, using plant butter and flax eggs or aquafaba as egg replacements. The version here uses oat milk, which behaves most similarly to whole milk in cake batters, and a flax egg for binding. The drizzle technique is unchanged from the classic; the crust formation depends on the ratio of sugar to lemon juice rather than the presence of egg.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before applying the drizzle; wrap well and freeze for up to 2 months. Defrost, then drizzle.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for 3 days; flavour is best on day 2.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 180°C or fan 160°C; ready when a skewer comes out clean

content.text: Vegan lemon drizzle produces the same moist, lemon-sharp loaf as the dairy version. A flax egg binds the batter; oat milk replicates the behaviour of whole milk. The essential step, pouring the warm lemon drizzle over the hot cake straight from the oven, is the same as the classic. Don't wait until the cake cools; a warm cake absorbs the drizzle deeper and sets the crust better.

items.prepNote: mixed with 3 tbsp water; leave 5 min to gel

content.text: Make the flax egg and bake

Mix the ground flaxseed with 3 tablespoons of water and leave for 5 minutes until gelatinous. Preheat the oven to 180°C conventional (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin. Beat the vegan butter and sugar together until pale. Add the flax egg and the lemon zest and beat again. Fold in the flour and baking powder alternately with the oat milk in two additions. Spoon into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

Mix the lemon juice and granulated sugar (don't dissolve the sugar, you want the crystals for the crust). When the cake comes out of the oven, prick the surface all over with a skewer, then pour the lemon and sugar mixture over immediately while the cake is still hot. The sugar soaks in partially and remains partially granular on the surface, forming the characteristic crust. Leave the cake to cool completely in the tin before turning out.
